text:
刷到一个图表 skill：「lieflat-charts」，两个半月 5.8k 星，推荐的人不少，我安装和使用后的结论是：
经常要给公众号、报告配图表的，直接装，出图是设计师水平，对外商用要找作者授权。

1）出图速度很快：一条命令装完，说句话就出图，一张约一分钟。第一张图我就知道他不一样，标题不是"使用时长统计"，是"Claude Code 占每周用时的 45.5%"，他把结论写进标题，黑白灰，脚注连四舍五入的口径都交代了。
2）很聪明，并不是无脑套模板。喂他一份数据，他先讲选型理由：竖排标签放不下完整产品名，所以换成刻度柱状图。这组数 9800 配 260，差 40 倍，图表断轴的问题很好的规避了，9800 那根完整冲天，柱顶的数据标签很完美。
3）长文字排版有惊喜。 11 个字的"自动驾驶感知算法工程师"，他不竖排硬塞，标签挪到条形上方横排，一个字没溢出。如果你对配色不满意，提示词直接说，改得很到位。
4）同一份数据不带 skill 裸画，五根条五个颜色，没有数据标签，没有来源行，带上他，就是编辑级的图。
5）邪修玩法：把他塞进 PPT skill，治好 PPT 图表的土；整篇文章丢给他，他自己理解内容出配图。
如果有一键导出 PNG 就极度完美。
经常要配图表的，可以无脑直接装，留意对外商用授权就好。

text:
如果你生活在加拿大，想提前退休，每个月需要$5,000加币生活费，需要多少资产？

答案：大约50万—55万加币。

核心就是用高现金流 Covered Call ETF：
$HDIV：加拿大市场为主，年化分派率约10%
$HYLD：美国市场为主，年化约12%
$EQCL：全球股票配置，年化约11%
HDIV、HYLD已经运行超过3年，EQCL也即将满3年。更重要的是，这三只ETF自成立以来都保持了按月派息记录，没有中断过，非常稳定的现金流来源，比你上班还要稳。

按照目前大约11%的综合分派率，55万加币每年可以产生约6万现金流，也就是每月$5,000左右。

而如果这是你唯一的收入来源，由于Covered Call ETF股息分派中会包含股息、资本利得和ROC等成分，实际税负通常会比同等工资收入低很多。

这就是我喜欢高股息ETF的原因：不用每天卖股票，钱每个月自动进账户，现金流非常有规律。同时你初始投入的55万本金也会随着市场慢慢上涨，不用担心本金侵蚀。对于追求退休现金流的人来说，这是一种非常值得研究的方案。

text:
骨灰级的忠告，看过以后大彻大悟，放过自己。

1. 这世界其实就你一个人，你在，世界就在，你不在，世界就消失了，所以请欣赏和热爱自己。。

2. 这一句直接封神：你面前有一个杯子，你喝水，它就是水杯；你抽烟，它就是烟灰缸；你插花，它就是花瓶。杯子本身，其实它什么也不是，这叫空性。你用它来干什么，它就是什么，这叫妙用。你非要坚持，它一定就是杯子，这叫住相。为此，你不惜和别人争论抬杠，这叫我执。结果，你抬杠有了情绪和谩骂，这叫烦恼。最后，你对这个人产生了反感，这叫偏见。然后，也就明白了，这个世界，其实没有别人，只有你自己。你在时，世界就跟着存在，你走后，世界就跟着消失。那些别人，那些纠缠，那些执着，那些控制，不过都是你内心，跟自己起的各种纠缠。于是，你就又明白了那句话：本来无一物，何处惹尘埃。

3. 内耗，就是没结果的自己跟自己较劲。焦虑，就是自己吓自己，把天想塌了。抑郁，就是自己不放过自己，一头扎进废墟里不出来。

4. 人生所有的机遇，都藏在恐惧里。

5. 这个世界没有真相，只有视角。

6. 别人嘴里的你不是你，你眼中的自己也不是你，你眼中的别人才是你自己。

7. 苏轼死前最后一句话：着力即差。卖力得来的都不算好的。

8. 正因为你不知道你是你，所以你才是你；一旦你知道了，你便不再是原来的你。

9. 不要跟重要的人计较不重要的事，不要跟不重要的人计较重要的事！

10. 务必珍惜身体。钱和照料，家人尚可帮你解决，但疾病的痛苦，只能独自承受。

11. 别人的认可，是最廉价的枷锁。

12. 人生不是只可以往上走，还可以四处走走。

13. 任何一种关系走得太近，都是一场灾难。

14. 家庭的第一原理是经济，而不是感情。职场的第一原理是功劳，而不是苦劳。人脉的第一原理是资源互换，而不是卑微讨好。爱情的第一原理是筛选，而不是培养。养老的第一原理是金钱，而不是依赖子女。

15. 有人喜欢吃辣椒，是因为辣椒辣，有人不喜欢吃辣椒，也是因为辣椒辣，所以这个世界没有所谓的真相，只有各自的视角。

16. 允许亲人撞南墙，看着朋友走弯路，目送爱人进坑，不是想害他们，而是说教会引起别人的仇恨，疼痛才是最好的老师。劝人从良，教人赚钱，帮人避坑，听着是在帮助他们，在积德，其实是在消耗自己的能量和运气，不要高估自己的能力也不要低估蠢人的执念，更不要介入别人的因果！

17. 除了父母，有血缘关系的兄弟姐妹以外，无论是谁对你的“好”，都有可能是装出来的，但TA对你的“恶”，一定是最真实无比的。所以不要光看别人对你好有多高的上线，要看TA对你的恶有多低的下限。

18. 上班让我感到最可怕的地方是：它居然让我因为期盼退休而期待衰老，让我完全不珍惜我剩余人生里最年轻的每一天，总想着周一到周五赶紧过去，可是一周又一周，突然反应过来：这流逝的是我的生命啊！

19. 钱没了可以再挣，工作没了可以再找，朋友没了可以再交，爱情没了可以再谈。你生来就一无所有，何惧从头再来？水到绝境是瀑布，人到绝境是重生，人生这道难题，怎么选都有遗憾。

20.千人同茶不同味，万人同道不同心。有人理解我之幸，无人理解我独行。知我者谓我心忧，不知我者谓我何求。世间万物皆可有，唯有懂字最难求。

个人 Vibe Coding 工具很容易选，提效也很直观，但从一个人变成一个组、多个组的团队，从个人 Vibe 一个自娱自乐的小项目，到支撑上亿用户量的企业级项目，中间的 gap 还是极其巨大！

阿里官方在正在进行的云栖大会 “智启原生 研见未来” 阿里巴巴集团 AI Native 研发实践论坛上，正式发布了「AI Native 研发范式实践手册」

68 页的实践手册，从阿里内部三个真实业务实践案例出发，讲述了不同团队研发范式演进路径中的实际探索与反思。

从这些案例中提炼出五个共性挑战：环境与验证驱动、平台能力升级、提效度量、数字员工和组织配套，尝试回答研发流程、协作方式和组织设计层面正在发生的结构性变化。

最后，进一步展开 企业级 AI 研发基础设施的技术全景：从 Harness 框架、企业知识库、工具体系（MCP / Skill / CLI），到 Sandbox 与 Coding 环境、身份与权限、生产安全 Guardrail 以及可观测能力，进而阐述让 Agent 从“能写代码”走向“可靠交付”所需要的系统性工程建设。

text:
太牛逼了，鱼总居然把推特一年 40 万+ 变现公开了，这么细的东西我是真不太敢发😅。。。

我就先陪一张今年部分海外收入吧，具体细节先不公开了，以后讲😂

X变现这块还得看鱼总，一年从 0 涨到 6.3 万粉：
商单 55-60%，联盟分佣 30-35%，官方收益 5-10%

我和鱼总在 X 变现方面思路差不多，或者说在 X 上，或者自媒体，真赚到钱的基本都这样：
号需要跟真实的变现需要绑在一起，为了流量做流量，除了流量啥也没有（其实，都是细节......）。

干货太多了，刚学习了一下，我来给大家详细讲一讲：
1、涨粉 = 曝光 × 转化
被别人 @、被大V转发，转化率最高，等于有人替你背书；曝光很大却不涨粉，多半是主页没接住。

2、回复最重要，作者自己下场回复权重最高
划走、点不感兴趣、拉黑都算扣分，硬塞标签、卡整点发都没用。怀疑被限流，设置里的 Under the Hood 能自己查。

3、前期千万别进互关群，也别刚发两三条就挂推广链接，很容易被当成营销号。

4、商单当干货写，数据好下一单就能涨价
联盟别等商家上门，主动找自己在用的工具谈，一篇卡类教程就能带来 1000-2000 美元分成。

5、社群和课程他反而不推荐，交付太重，做不好还伤 IP（我也是这样想的，收益很难做高，而且交付太重了）。

兄弟们，别管是推特还是其他各种平台，做起来吧！如果你能坚持三个月肯定会很大的收获！

Gnos 是一个开源的 AI 教学工具，装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类编码 Agent，就能把它变成一个会排课的老师。

先说想学什么、打算学多深、每周有多少时间，它会参考大学课程大纲、教材和官方文档排一条学习路线，再把第一课做出来。

GitHub：https://t.co/ORBrgiUALj

讲课不光是文字，会按内容挑形式，图解、可交互的模拟、带配音的动画讲解、PDF 讲义都能出，整门课还能在浏览器里打开学。

学的过程中，它会记下我们试过什么、思路在哪卡住，还把掌握程度分成看过讲解、有提示能做、独立能做 3 档，后面的课跟着调整。

把看懂和会做分开记，这点我挺认同，自学最容易高估自己的就是这里。

仓库里的示例课是从强化学习一路讲到 GRPO，拿来啃这类硬骨头挺合适。

text:
推荐这期 Latent Space 的播客，请的是 Claude Code 的 Thariq。92 分钟，信息密度很高

几个我听完比较关注的点

- 关于 prompt：Thariq 说 prompting 是元技能，核心在两个，一个是你对具体模型的心智模型及模型的能力边界是否专业，二是你对所解决问题的领域词汇掌握是否足够到精准描述问题和需求。（我想到一个很残酷的事情，很多人都期待能用AI做到自己不了解的事，但领域词汇的匮乏，注定prompt会比专业大哥们差）。

- Brain, Hands, and Surface UI：Anthropic 在把 Claude 拆成三层。1，云端 brain 一直在跑，能开子 agent，子 agent 之间能互通；2，hands 是执行端，可以是本地、云端、沙箱；3，surface 用 Artifact 做界面，数据库是同一份，但UI层千人千面。

- 做两头，不做中间（Thariq 管这叫杠铃策略）：围绕 agent 搭的工具链过时很快，方向还不可预测。所以投入只放两头。一头是安全、权限、沙箱，不管模型怎么迭代都需要，做重；另一头是日常工作流脚本、prompt 模板，下一代模型可能自己就会了，做轻，能用就行。最亏的是中间那层，比如花几个月精心搭一套多 agent 协作的编排框架，结果新模型一出来，它自己就会调度子 agent、自己会汇报了。这层投入说没就没，因为它还没到"不可替代"那个层次。（这点不是那么同意，有机会细说）

result.text:
推荐这期 Latent Space 的播客，请的是 Claude Code 的 Thariq。92 分钟，信息密度很高

几个我听完比较关注的点

- 关于 prompt：Thariq 说 prompting 是元技能，核心在两个，一个是你对具体模型的心智模型及模型的能力边界是否专业，二是你对所解决问题的领域词汇掌握是否足够到精准描述问题和需求。（我想到一个很残酷的事情，很多人都期待能用AI做到自己不了解的事，但领域词汇的匮乏，注定prompt会比专业大哥们差）。

- Brain, Hands, and Surface UI：Anthropic 在把 Claude 拆成三层。1，云端 brain 一直在跑，能开子 agent，子 agent 之间能互通；2，hands 是执行端，可以是本地、云端、沙箱；3，surface 用 Artifact 做界面，数据库是同一份，但UI层千人千面。

- 做两头，不做中间（Thariq 管这叫杠铃策略）：围绕 agent 搭的工具链过时很快，方向还不可预测。所以投入只放两头。一头是安全、权限、沙箱，不管模型怎么迭代都需要，做重；另一头是日常工作流脚本、prompt 模板，下一代模型可能自己就会了，做轻，能用就行。最亏的是中间那层，比如花几个月精心搭一套多 agent 协作的编排框架，结果新模型一出来，它自己就会调度子 agent、自己会汇报了。这层投入说没就没，因为它还没到"不可替代"那个层次。（这点不是那么同意，有机会细说）

text:
微软搞的一个去中心化多AI框架：Agensh，去掉“AI大管家”，让最多1024个Agent自协作，自己商量、分工、干活

结果是人越多越快，128个AI半小时就突破的进度，1个AI 两小时都达不到，有意思的是AI还自发长出了组织能力

随着AI数量增加，涌现出了类似人类社会的现象：
8个AI：先约定接口，然后各自独立开发

32个AI：出现多人评审，发现bug会撤回批准、要求返工

当128个AI：出现专业分工和标准化流程，还发明了一套整合协议（更新+测试+发哈希验证），后来被其他AI复用和修订

当1024个AI：出现专职的“整合者”角色，某个AI失败后会有专长者接手，组织不再依赖任何单一个体

现在的多AI系统一般是“一个老板带一群员工”，老板要负责派活、协调、汇总

Agensh的解法是，不要老板，每个AI都拿到同样的任务说明，然后循环做五件事：

1、看进展，项目做到哪了？别人发现了什么？
2、认领任务，并公开声明（撞车了就和对方私下协商）
3、动手干活，写代码、跑测试
4、自检结果，不达标就继续修
5、提交合并，提交Pull Request，把成果并入主干

配套的是三件套基础设施，很像GitHub工作流：共享工作区（Git管代码和合并冲突）、消息接口（频道公告+私聊，类似Slack）、共享上下文（记录事实、失败教训、任务认领的团队Wiki）

这对费时费力的长时工程倒是一种新解法。在把单个模型做大和让单个模型多想一会儿之间给出了第三条路，固定模型不变，增加Agent数量，让整体能力提升

#Agensh #Agent

别再花几千块买投资课了，这份免费的《投资入门指南》可能更适合新手。

徐冲浪老师把自己的投资知识体系直接开源了。

从美股、期权到 Crypto，不是教你追热点、找暴富密码，而是帮你从零搭起一套完整的投资认知框架。

很多新手不是学不会投资，而是一开始就被碎片化的信息带偏了。

如果你连股票、期权这些东西到底该按什么顺序学都没搞清楚，这份资料值得从头啃一遍。

项目地址：https://t.co/BpnMy5zIdp

非投资建议，仅为学习资料分享。

quotedTweet.text:
华尔街不会主动告诉你的10个免费美股网站

别再只会刷财经新闻了。

很多时候，当你看到一条新闻冲进去的时候，真正影响股价的数据，专业投资者可能早就在跟踪。

分享10个值得收藏的网站👇

1、MacroMicro：把宏观数据直接变成图

如果你看FRED觉得太硬核，可以试试MacroMicro。

通胀、利率、美债、美元、就业、制造业、流动性等大量宏观指标都做成了可视化图表。

研究“为什么美股最近涨/跌”，经常能在这里找到宏观线索。

https://t.co/lIox5txzq0

2、New York Fed：盯美元流动性

纽约联储官网是很多人容易忽略的宝藏。

SOFR、回购市场、纽约联储公开市场操作等数据，都可以直接查。

尤其当市场开始讨论“流动性”“降息”“资金面”的时候，别只看别人解读，可以回来找原始数据。

https://t.co/C0PyZ4iBzl

3、Federal Reserve：直接看美联储

研究美股，美联储官网其实应该放进收藏夹。

FOMC声明、会议纪要、经济预测、利率决议以及美联储官员相关信息，都可以找到。

不要只看新闻标题里的“鹰派”“鸽派”，原文往往比二手解读更重要。

https://t.co/vi3zz8xl2F

4、FINRA：查市场监管和交易数据

FINRA是美国金融业监管局。

除了监管信息之外，还能查询部分市场统计、OTC和交易相关数据。

当你研究一些成交异常、做空或者市场结构问题时，它比普通财经网站更接近数据源头。

https://t.co/1UTUXi4COS

5、ChartExchange：研究做空和市场数据

这个网站很多普通投资者没用过。

可以辅助查看Short Volume、Fails-to-Deliver等市场数据，一些股票还能进一步观察借券相关信息。

研究热门股、逼空概念股时，比只看社交媒体喊“Short Squeeze”靠谱得多。

https://t.co/BMfTF60ata

6、AlphaQuery：查波动率和期权数据

如果你开始研究期权，这个网站值得收藏。

可以辅助查看股票的历史波动率、隐含波动率以及部分期权统计数据。

有时候股价没怎么动，但期权市场已经开始给未来波动重新定价了。

https://t.co/nLESJsVhY5

7、StockCharts：老牌技术分析网站

界面看起来可能没有那么“新”，但工具很成熟。

趋势、均线、RSI、MACD、相对强弱等技术分析都能做。

特别适合同时观察指数、行业ETF和个股之间的强弱关系。

https://t.co/yAojQD7ZQs

8、HedgeFollow：看机构13F持仓

想知道大型基金公开披露了哪些股票，可以看看HedgeFollow。

text:
我发现一个可以暂时 无限 薅 GPT-6-Astra 的方法。

就是去使用OpenAI 新出的云电脑助手，里面内置的默认模型就是 GPT-6-Astra 系列。用它在云电脑跑任务，现在是不消耗本身的订阅额度的。

但是如果你让 DOT 对本地Codex 发送任务指令，那任务的消耗额度还是扣订阅里面的。

所以其实你就可以把能用云电脑跑的任务，全丢过去，用的还是 6-Astra 的模型，还不消耗额度，用来搞这种白膜运镜或者其他的东西，这一个月下来估计能省不少钱。

干净去试试吧

text:
感谢@yifanxu_ephai 分享这篇文章，我在阅读的过程中发现自己缺乏不少分布式方面的知识，导致理解这篇文章比较慢一些，为了帮助大家理解，在这里分享一些会涉及到的分布式方面的知识，也是学习Agent Infra所需要的知识（因为涉及的内容比较多，我会持续添加）：
1.Stateful vs Stateless
Stateful：之前的运行状态是由程序自身记忆的

Stateless：之前的运行状态是由外部记忆的

假设我们有一个计数功能，从0开始，每秒数字加1。

对于stateful来说，如果这个计数功能崩了，那么重新启动的话，计数还是从0开始；

对于stateless来说，如果这个计数功能崩了，那么重新启动的话，计数还是从崩之前继续。

对于Agent来说，为什么runtime做成stateless比较重要，尤其是长任务？

因为随着agent的执行，会积攒很多上下文信息（包括和用户的对话内容，调用了哪些工具等等），如果是用stateful，那么这些信息都是存储在agent runtime进程中，如果进程挂了，则这些重要的信息也会随之丢失，再起一个新的agent进程也无法找回丢失的上下文信息。

而如果是stateless的话，则这些信息存储在进程之外，即使进程崩了，再起一个新的进程也能通过session_id寻找到原始的信息。

在执行长任务过程中，进程崩溃，pod被驱逐，电脑重启这些情况都是会发生的。所以，做成stateless是很有必要的，且这些信息也要能做到分布式存储，避免丢失。

🧭 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸. The Chief of Staff prompt from @trevin has it read your last 90 days, brief you on facts vs guesses, then ask you questions five at a time. 𝘚𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘥𝘶𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘯𝘣𝘰𝘢𝘳𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨

text:
Jev for RAG, clearly explained!

Hybrid search gives you a shortlist. It does not decide which passages contain evidence, which are merely adjacent, or whether the evidence is strong enough to answer.

That missing judgment is where Jev fits.

Jev sits between retrieval and generation. It does not replace BM25, embeddings, or the LLM. It evaluates the candidates they produce before those candidates enter the context window.

→ Retrieve wide

Combine dense and keyword search, then merge the results with reciprocal rank fusion. This gives Jev a broad candidate pool, such as the top 20 passages shown in the visual.

Retrieval still sets the ceiling. If the right passage is missing from this shortlist, Jev cannot recover it.

→ Judge every candidate together

Send the query as Jev’s state. For each candidate, ask a typed yes-or-no question such as “Does C7 help answer this query?”

Jev evaluates every question in one packed request and returns a calibrated probability for each passage. This avoids making a separate model call for every query-passage pair.

→ Let code apply the threshold

Your application compares each probability with a threshold. Candidates above it continue to the LLM. Everything below it is removed before generation.

Jev makes the fuzzy judgment. Code remains responsible for the actual decision.

→ Gate the entire answer

The same request can check whether the retained passages make the query answerable. It can also flag signs of prompt injection inside a candidate.

If answerability falls below the threshold, the application can skip the LLM and return “not in the documents.” The injection score should remain a filtering signal, not a security boundary.

The result is a cleaner division of work.

Hybrid search retrieves broadly. Jev reranks, filters, and decides whether sufficient evidence exists. The LLM writes only from the passages that survive.

Jev’s value here is not simply moving passages up or down a list. It turns relevance into an explicit probability that your application can inspect, threshold, and act on.

To summarise:

- Retrieval finds the candidates.
- Jev decides what deserves context.
- The LLM writes the grounded answer.

----
I also built an open-source project showing how to use Jev as a judge for AI observability with Comet Opik.

It evaluates support traces for groundedness, request coverage, action honesty, and helpfulness, then records the results as an auditable experiment.

You can explore the project here: https://t.co/XVmpg6ldHT

My article on how Jev works is quoted below.

text:
09/28 今天半导体集体下跌，很多人懵了，AI 又不行了吗？ $MRVL -4%, $COHR -6%, $CRDO -8%，而安全股大涨。今天背后的逻辑其实很简单：周末媒体集中炒了又炒了一波 AI 放缓的冷饭

研发暂停（？） → 云厂少建数据中心 → MRVL、Coherent 被砍单。我的观点恰恰相反，当补全了安全策略之后，模型训练和推理会跑得更快

1/ 我觉得今天市场又在交易一个夸张的错误逻辑，可能会给我们带来机会。

逻辑错误主要是：OpenAI 暂停部分研发，怎么就一路推导成了光模块要被砍单？我认为不太合理，有逻辑 gap

我梳理周末前后 3 个时间点，3 条证据，2 个我在等的机会

 2/ 先把时间捋一下：

① 9/25 周五：OpenAI 更新报告，披露 9/20 的新安全事故及暂停安排。[1] 
② 9/26 周六：Fortune 跟进，“再次暂停”继续发酵。[2]
③ 9/28 周一：AI 硬件股承压，财经报道直接把 MRVL 下跌与这次暂停联系起来。[3]

新事故，又把“AI 放缓”的旧叙事炒热了。

3/ 我为什么觉得市场可能推过头了？看 3 条证据：

1. 暂停有范围。官方针对的是最强模型的训练、评估和带工具的推理，不能扩大成整个 AI 行业停工。[1] 此外，我发现市场认知对于训练和推理还是没有分开啊

2. 官方写了补网络隔离、做红队测试，以及重启新训练的安排。恢复日期没给，但这份报告没有宣布削减算力采购。[1] 

3. 安全股同时走强就能印证这个观点，PANW 午盘一度涨约 4%。我的理解是，资金也在押注：AI 继续用，只是安全的钱得补上。[4]

4/ 为什么硬件股又挨打，我在等待什么？
硬件股在买未来的扩建速度，price in了未来，这个毫无疑问

我不相信整个 AI 产业会因此停下来。我的押注是：整改后继续跑, 而且会跑得更快。这个判断可能错，所以我在等两个机会：

① Agent 安全。谁能替 AI 管权限、限制越界，谁就可能拿到新增预算，这就是我之前喜欢 $OKTA 的原因。但股价已经涨了，下一步要看新增合同，不能只追故事。

② 我更关心的 $MRVL。10/6 投资者日快到了，我想看客户项目和光互联收入的时间表能否更清楚。[5]

如果继续回调，但订单和指引没变，只会把它当作一个好机会

09/28 今天半导体集体下跌，很多人懵了，AI 又不行了吗？ $MRVL -4%, $COHR -6%, $CRDO -8%，而安全股大涨。今天背后的逻辑其实很简单：周末媒体集中炒了又炒了一波 AI 放缓的冷饭

研发暂停（？） → 云厂少建数据中心 → MRVL、Coherent 被砍单。我的观点恰恰相反，当补全了安全策略之后，模型训练和推理会跑得更快

1/ 我觉得今天市场又在交易一个夸张的错误逻辑，可能会给我们带来机会。

逻辑错误主要是：OpenAI 暂停部分研发，怎么就一路推导成了光模块要被砍单？我认为不太合理，有逻辑 gap

我梳理周末前后 3 个时间点，3 条证据，2 个我在等的机会

 2/ 先把时间捋一下：

① 9/25 周五：OpenAI 更新报告，披露 9/20 的新安全事故及暂停安排。[1] 
② 9/26 周六：Fortune 跟进，“再次暂停”继续发酵。[2]
③ 9/28 周一：AI 硬件股承压，财经报道直接把 MRVL 下跌与这次暂停联系起来。[3]

新事故，又把“AI 放缓”的旧叙事炒热了。

3/ 我为什么觉得市场可能推过头了？看 3 条证据：

1. 暂停有范围。官方针对的是最强模型的训练、评估和带工具的推理，不能扩大成整个 AI 行业停工。[1] 此外，我发现市场认知对于训练和推理还是没有分开啊

2. 官方写了补网络隔离、做红队测试，以及重启新训练的安排。恢复日期没给，但这份报告没有宣布削减算力采购。[1] 

3. 安全股同时走强就能印证这个观点，PANW 午盘一度涨约 4%。我的理解是，资金也在押注：AI 继续用，只是安全的钱得补上。[4]

4/ 为什么硬件股又挨打，我在等待什么？
硬件股在买未来的扩建速度，price in了未来，这个毫无疑问

我不相信整个 AI 产业会因此停下来。我的押注是：整改后继续跑, 而且会跑得更快。这个判断可能错，所以我在等两个机会：

① Agent 安全。谁能替 AI 管权限、限制越界，谁就可能拿到新增预算，这就是我之前喜欢 $OKTA 的原因。但股价已经涨了，下一步要看新增合同，不能只追故事。

② 我更关心的 $MRVL。10/6 投资者日快到了，我想看客户项目和光互联收入的时间表能否更清楚。[5]

如果继续回调，但订单和指引没变，只会把它当作一个好机会

text:
Pi 配上 Subagent，有点 Multi-Agent 的味道了🔥

推荐一个最近在玩的插件：jopqior/pi-subagents

可以直接在 Pi 里面拉起多个独立的 Subagent，而且不是再开几个 CLI 子进程，是直接跑在 Pi 自己的 Runtime 里面

1、每个 Subagent 都是独立的

可以有自己的 Model、Thinking、Tools、System Prompt 和 Session

比如主 Agent 负责整体任务，再单独开一个 Research、一个 Coding、一个 Review，各干各的。

2、可以并行跑，而且中途还能管

默认可以同时跑多个 Subagent，后台干活的时候你还能继续跟主 Agent 聊。

跑偏了可以 Steering，跑完了还能 Resume 原来的 Session，不是一次性问完就没了。

3、不同 Subagent 还能分配不同模型

配合 pi-subagents-model-selector，可以让：

Research → Gemini
Coding → Claude
Review → GPT

谁适合干什么就分给谁，不需要所有 Agent 都用一个模型。

这个插件火起来也有一段时间了，最新版本也更新了 MCP，现在是子线程也火起来了

连 PI 慢慢更新的跟 OMP 一样了，那我还不如直接去隔壁使用 OMP🤣

quotedTweet.text:
Pi 0.99.0 发布，还更新了挺多东西的🔥

这次可以说是一个比较大版本的更新，更新的几个点我都比较在意，我把它整理出来了

1、MCP 正式内置，但是做法很 Pi

这次直接加入 Codemode、MCP 和 Tool Search。

模型可以自己写 JavaScript，在 QuickJS 沙箱里一次调用多个 Tool，甚至并行执行。

更关键的是，MCP 一大堆 Tool 默认不用全部塞进 Context，需要的时候再搜索、再调用。

明显还是在控制 Context 膨胀。

2、模型也开始可以动态路由了

新增 Virtual Models。

你在 /model 里选的可以只是一个“虚拟模型”，真正执行时，每一轮请求都可以根据任务自动切到不同模型和 Thinking Level。

简单理解：

简单任务用便宜模型，复杂任务再切强模型。

而且 Pi 会记录最后到底是谁干的、花了多少钱。

3、ChatGPT 订阅现在可以直接登录 Pi

直接：

/login openai

就可以用 ChatGPT Subscription 接 OpenAI Provider。

以前的 OpenAI Codex Provider 甚至已经被标成 legacy，这个对订阅用户还是挺实用的。

4、还加入了 Classifier Model

现在 Jev、llama.cpp 模型都可以不负责聊天，只负责快速判断：

这个任务属于哪一类？
要不要放行？
应该交给哪个模型？

再配合 Virtual Model，已经很像：

先用小模型判断 → 再自动分配真正干活的模型。

另外这版还有 Image Generation Runtime、Claude Sonnet 5.5、System Theme，以及长 Session Streaming CPU 占用优化。

这个版本最大的改变是把MCP放进去了，这是一种妥协，也是一种改变，希望慢慢地Pi保留初心的前提下能继续发展

result.text:
Pi 0.99.0 发布，还更新了挺多东西的🔥

这次可以说是一个比较大版本的更新，更新的几个点我都比较在意，我把它整理出来了

1、MCP 正式内置，但是做法很 Pi

这次直接加入 Codemode、MCP 和 Tool Search。

模型可以自己写 JavaScript，在 QuickJS 沙箱里一次调用多个 Tool，甚至并行执行。

更关键的是，MCP 一大堆 Tool 默认不用全部塞进 Context，需要的时候再搜索、再调用。

明显还是在控制 Context 膨胀。

2、模型也开始可以动态路由了

新增 Virtual Models。

你在 /model 里选的可以只是一个“虚拟模型”，真正执行时，每一轮请求都可以根据任务自动切到不同模型和 Thinking Level。

简单理解：

简单任务用便宜模型，复杂任务再切强模型。

而且 Pi 会记录最后到底是谁干的、花了多少钱。

3、ChatGPT 订阅现在可以直接登录 Pi

直接：

/login openai

就可以用 ChatGPT Subscription 接 OpenAI Provider。

以前的 OpenAI Codex Provider 甚至已经被标成 legacy，这个对订阅用户还是挺实用的。

4、还加入了 Classifier Model

现在 Jev、llama.cpp 模型都可以不负责聊天，只负责快速判断：

这个任务属于哪一类？
要不要放行？
应该交给哪个模型？

再配合 Virtual Model，已经很像：

先用小模型判断 → 再自动分配真正干活的模型。

另外这版还有 Image Generation Runtime、Claude Sonnet 5.5、System Theme，以及长 Session Streaming CPU 占用优化。

这个版本最大的改变是把MCP放进去了，这是一种妥协，也是一种改变，希望慢慢地Pi保留初心的前提下能继续发展

Muse architecture, this is how Meta’s assistant works

It’s not difficult to get this information. A couple of questions to Muse and it will describe the architecture itself

My guess is that something close to this has to be part of its system prompt, since it defines the full scope of what Muse can do and where its limits are.

The important parts:
- An agent loop: understand, plan, act, verify, reply

- A persistent Linux VM with terminal and internet access

- Files, scripts, and tool execution

- A live Chromium browser with persistent logins

- Connected services like Gmail, Calendar, Spotify, Threads, Instagram, health data, and devices

- Background work with subagents, scheduled jobs, and event hooks

- Memory for preferences, projects, people, goals, and commitments

- Media and document generation

- Safeguards around publishing, sending, buying, credentials, and source verification

I’ll keep asking this every once in a while to see what changes and what gets added

text:
整个科技圈风向都在卷大企业 AI， 结果 @Meta 的 @AIatMeta AI 掌门人 @alexandr_wang 刚刚发推说他们后台发现，把 Muse 用得最猛的， 竟然是修水管的、开农场的、开杂货店和开小餐馆的老板……
上线两周，早期用户里竟然有 1/3 直接把它绑定了商业账号。
今天 Meta 顺水推舟，直接上线了 Muse for Small Business， 一口气甩出 22 个官方连接器： Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks、Canva、Zoom、Slack…… 把小商家的全套数字牛马直接做实了。

我把背后的逻辑和搞钱启示用大白话给大家拆一下👇
━━
1｜最反直觉的现象：用 AI 最狠的不是大厂，是个体户
大厂做 AI 喜欢去找世界 500 强做大单子， 但真实世界里，最缺时间的是那些“一人身兼八职”的小老板。
官方案例里有个爱荷华州开杂货店的大叔： 每周工作 65 个小时，店里进货是他、管账是他、做促销是他、处理退款还是他。 他缺的根本不是点子，是时间。
以前大家以为 Muse 只是个帮宅男比价订外卖的玩具， 结果这些小老板早就拿它去回客户邮件、查库存、算账了。

2｜这 22 个连接器，到底解决了啥？
做过独立电商、自媒体或者小生意的朋友都懂这个痛点： 每天要在 8 个后台之间来回切—— 看销量去 Shopify，查退款去 Stripe，做海报去 Canva，记账去 QuickBooks，开会去 Zoom，内部沟通去 Slack。
现在 Muse 把它全收拢到一个对话框里： ▫️查账退款：不用登录 Stripe 后台，直接对它说“把昨天争议的那笔单子退了”，它核对完调接口执行 ▫️内容与营销：识别你的产品库存和品牌调性，直接调用 Canva 生成下周促销海报，一键推到 Instagram 商业主页 ▫️客户与日程：给它配个专属邮箱，客户发来的询价、改期邮件，它在后台看懂日历直接起草回复
一句话：它不是让你去学一个新软件，而是把你手上所有的 SaaS 变成听话的后台。

3｜Meta 这步棋最狠的地方在哪？
Facebook 和 Instagram 上有整整 2 亿小微商家。 这是全球最大的个体老板聚集地。
Meta 根本不需要跟微软、谷歌去抢那些复杂的企业级大单， 它只要让这 2 亿小老板在手机上： “少雇一个客服、少花 2 小时对账、少切 5 个软件”。
而且最聪明的是它的安全机制： 所有涉及扣费、退款、对外公开发布的操作，AI 负责跑腿起草，最后一步依然要人点确认。 这就是我们常说的“人管方向和钱包，AI 管繁琐和流程”。

4｜对我们普通人和超级个体意味着什么？
一人公司（One-Person Company）过去最大的瓶颈，不是你不会做核心业务，而是被杂事活活拖死。 你懂做视频，但你不想花时间回商务邮件； 你懂写代码，但你讨厌天天去处理发票和对账。
当 AI Agent 开始长出连接现实商业系统的手（Connectors）： 以前需要 3 个人支撑的微型工作室， 以后可能真的 1 个人加一个配置好的 Personal AI 就能跑起来。

5｜照例泼盆冷水
▫️这套连接器目前深度绑定的是海外生态（Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks 等），国内主流的微店、淘宝、微信支付等生态目前还没打通； ▫️多平台授权意味着你的商业数据、客户往来都在被 AI 扫描，哪些权限给、哪些不给，依然得有边界； ▫️复杂业务逻辑的容错率低，账目核算依然需要人工定期复核，别做甩手掌柜。
━━
过去我们讨论 AI，总觉得它是高高在上的算力和算法。
 但今天 Alexandr Wang 这条推说明了一件事： AI 落地最快、最扎实的地方， 永远是帮街角那家店的老板，把今晚下班的时间提前两个小时。
开源了自定义接入平台（https://t.co/GGtFihiFNC）。 如果国内也有一个 AI 能接通你所有的工作软件，你最想让它替你干掉哪个日常琐事？ https://t.co/zrRk2zy06N

一句话：它不是让你去学一个新软件，而是把你手上所有的 SaaS 变成听话的后台。

3｜Meta 这步棋最狠的地方在哪？
Facebook 和 Instagram 上有整整 2 亿小微商家。 这是全球最大的个体老板聚集地。
Meta 根本不需要跟微软、谷歌去抢那些复杂的企业级大单， 它只要让这 2 亿小老板在手机上： “少雇一个客服、少花 2 小时对账、少切 5 个软件”。
而且最聪明的是它的安全机制： 所有涉及扣费、退款、对外公开发布的操作，AI 负责跑腿起草，最后一步依然要人点确认。 这就是我们常说的“人管方向和钱包，AI 管繁琐和流程”。

4｜对我们普通人和超级个体意味着什么？
一人公司（One-Person Company）过去最大的瓶颈，不是你不会做核心业务，而是被杂事活活拖死。 你懂做视频，但你不想花时间回商务邮件； 你懂写代码，但你讨厌天天去处理发票和对账。
当 AI Agent 开始长出连接现实商业系统的手（Connectors）： 以前需要 3 个人支撑的微型工作室， 以后可能真的 1 个人加一个配置好的 Personal AI 就能跑起来。

5｜照例泼盆冷水
▫️这套连接器目前深度绑定的是海外生态（Shopify、Stripe、QuickBooks 等），国内主流的微店、淘宝、微信支付等生态目前还没打通； ▫️多平台授权意味着你的商业数据、客户往来都在被 AI 扫描，哪些权限给、哪些不给，依然得有边界； ▫️复杂业务逻辑的容错率低，账目核算依然需要人工定期复核，别做甩手掌柜。
━━
过去我们讨论 AI，总觉得它是高高在上的算力和算法。
 但今天 Alexandr Wang 这条推说明了一件事： AI 落地最快、最扎实的地方， 永远是帮街角那家店的老板，把今晚下班的时间提前两个小时。
开源了自定义接入平台（https://t.co/GGtFihiFNC）。 如果国内也有一个 AI 能接通你所有的工作软件，你最想让它替你干掉哪个日常琐事？ https://t.co/zrRk2zy06N

If you still think 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟱.𝟱 is only good for pretty animations and websites, try this:

"When someone comments GUIDE on any post, get their email, send my free guide."

Connect Opus 5.5 to Blotato, send it that line, and it builds the automation. Then test from another account: "Your own comments won't trigger it." After that you just post. Even on 𝗮𝗻 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗼, anyone who comments GUIDE gets the guide in their DMs, and anyone who wants to can leave you their email.

A lot of those "comment a keyword to get it" posts you keep seeing run on an automation like this.

继续伟大的开源了！！！最全的抖音生态工具箱ah-skill炸裂更新！！！我终于不用在闲鱼5000块找人帮我批量提取逐字稿了！！！！Codex半小时，就能提取150+视频内容，消耗TOKEN量是5x账号周限额的0.5%

如果说你也需要批量提取逐字稿，以前这件事儿需要大量的时间，现在一个博主主页链接分享给Codex，它就能把所有的逐字稿提取出来，效率奇高

1、给 Codex 一个博主主页，它先采公开作品目录
2、迅速逐条临时保存原片，用本机 Whisper 转机器逐字稿和带时间码的字幕
3、给我一份能搜索的合集和作品索引，自动路由obsidian建文件夹

以前做对标，视频看完就散了。现在要找一个开头、一个选题，或者看同一个博主反复讲什么，我能直接回到对应原片和逐字稿。

quotedTweet.text:
我有点懵了，兄弟们。。。。我好像真的发现AI做视频的流量密码了·····感觉可以这样日更1000条做矩阵了····

前段时间，我发了一条视频，24.66 万播放，1.21 万点赞，直接帮我涨了 2912 个粉丝，那如果我把这条已经验证过的爆款重新提炼、重新剪辑，再发到小号上，它还能不能继续帮我涨粉？而这件事只需要我把我爆过的内容，让AI当做素材给我进行切片就可以了

问了Codex给我推荐一下，他跟我说让我用用Fotor Agent @fotor_com，geo还是得相信啊，真的太快了，效果太好了，而且真的是又省token又省心啊！！！ 我把一条 7 分钟的口播丢进 Fotor Agent，只进行了一轮对话，它直接给我压成了 60 秒

重复的废话砍了，最吸引人的原句挑出来了，字幕也一起对齐了

以前剪这种长口播或者直播做切片，最耗时间的是你要从头到尾听一遍，判断哪里该留气口，哪里不用留，哪句话真正能留人，哪段删掉以后逻辑还不能断，这个判断过程太磨人了

我这次给 Fotor Agent 的要求其实非常简单：100个字左右的提示词就在视频里你们直接看就行，最后压进 60 秒，只跟它对话了4轮，我觉得这个效果就已经特别nice了

我觉得纯口播的素材太单调，它先问我要不要加空镜和关键词词卡，然后空镜、词卡、强调黄字，全部自动铺进时间线

而且！！！它生成完不会只丢给我一个 MP4 就跑了，所有字幕都能拖，字重、字号、行高、字距、颜色和不透明度都能直接改

哪一句识别得不对，我自己点开改就行，不需要再跟 AI 来回聊半天，真的兄弟们

这对做切片和矩阵号的人真的很实用 保留已经被数据验证过的观点，再重新组织钩子、重点和结构

如果你拿的是已经获得授权、或者明确允许二创的长视频，也别总想着只换个标题、裁一下画面就可以了，我最近发现先把真正有传播力的观点提炼出来，再补上你自己的解释、判断和结构，这才是有1+1>2的效果

原内容负责抓住人，你的判断负责让它变成一条新的内容，这才是二创最简单粗暴、也更能长期做下去的方式

Fotor Agent 能替你吃掉前面的粗剪和整理，有长视频切片需求的人，真的可以拿一条自己的素材去试一下

text:
jev + opus 5.5 for design is insane...

a launch video used to mean an agency, weeks of back and forth and a fat invoice.

now Opus 5.5 makes the video, the ad cuts and the landing page from one brief.

the video below: made in 3 minutes. at 0:09 it drops into edit mode - dot grid, selection handles, pixel sizes on every card - so you see exactly how it was built.

but most people get the same mid result: centered text, gradient background, everything fading in. That's Opus's default look when it has nothing to copy.

here's the pipeline that makes it look like an agency did it:

1. Build the brand brain first
→ logo, colors, fonts, screenshots of your real product, your best ad copy
→ have Opus turn it into a DESIGN.md. The video and the site both follow it

2. Steal a reference, don't describe one
→ pick 1-2 launch videos with the pacing you want
→ "make it like this" beats "make it modern and punchy" every time

3. Give it a renderer
→ install HyperFrames or Remotion: every scene is code, rendered straight to mp4
→ a change = one line and a re-render, not starting over

4. Use real components
→ buttons, cards and UI from 21st_dev instead of empty placeholder boxes
→ fake-looking UI is the fastest way to look cheap

5. Storyboard before motion
→ 3 storyboard options, you pick one, then one still per scene
→ fixing a still takes seconds, fixing a render takes a re-render

6. Run it as a 4-person team + jev
→ breakdown: pull pacing, type and transitions from the reference
→ storyboard: the 3 options and the stills
→ build: every scene in code, music, draft render
→ review: watch it second by second, list the problems, touch nothing
→ jev: scores every review note against DESIGN.md (fix now / later / skip) in milliseconds, so build only touches what matters

7. Cut the ads from the same project
→ same scenes, different hooks: pain first, result first, offer first
→ 9:16 for reels, 1:1 for feed, 16:9 for YouTube. No reshoots

8. Ship the landing page from the same DESIGN.md
→ the hero is a looping cut of the launch video
→ before launch: mobile, every button state, zero placeholder text

9. Give notes like a director
→ "slow this zoom by half", "hard cut here", "push in on the button"

jev + opus 5.5 for design is insane...

a launch video used to mean an agency, weeks of back and forth and a fat invoice.

now Opus 5.5 makes the video, the ad cuts and the landing page from one brief.

the video below: made in 3 minutes. at 0:09 it drops into edit mode - dot grid, selection handles, pixel sizes on every card - so you see exactly how it was built.

but most people get the same mid result: centered text, gradient background, everything fading in. That's Opus's default look when it has nothing to copy.

here's the pipeline that makes it look like an agency did it:

1. Build the brand brain first
→ logo, colors, fonts, screenshots of your real product, your best ad copy
→ have Opus turn it into a DESIGN.md. The video and the site both follow it

2. Steal a reference, don't describe one
→ pick 1-2 launch videos with the pacing you want
→ "make it like this" beats "make it modern and punchy" every time

3. Give it a renderer
→ install HyperFrames or Remotion: every scene is code, rendered straight to mp4
→ a change = one line and a re-render, not starting over

4. Use real components
→ buttons, cards and UI from 21st_dev instead of empty placeholder boxes
→ fake-looking UI is the fastest way to look cheap

5. Storyboard before motion
→ 3 storyboard options, you pick one, then one still per scene
→ fixing a still takes seconds, fixing a render takes a re-render

6. Run it as a 4-person team + jev
→ breakdown: pull pacing, type and transitions from the reference
→ storyboard: the 3 options and the stills
→ build: every scene in code, music, draft render
→ review: watch it second by second, list the problems, touch nothing
→ jev: scores every review note against DESIGN.md (fix now / later / skip) in milliseconds, so build only touches what matters

→ same scenes, different hooks: pain first, result first, offer first
→ 9:16 for reels, 1:1 for feed, 16:9 for YouTube. No reshoots

8. Ship the landing page from the same DESIGN.md
→ the hero is a looping cut of the launch video

text:
Netflix has more than 300 million subscribers around the world.

It spends billions of dollars every year on shows, movies, and the algorithm that decides what you see when you open t he app.

And here is the part almost nobody talks about: Netflix is betting that most of those 300 million people will never open the settings menu.

Not because the settings are secret. They are right there. But they are buried three taps deep, named in a way that makes them sound boring, and set by default to whatever is best for Netflix, not for you.

So I did something most people never do. I sat down and went through every single Netflix setting, one by one, on my phone, my laptop, and my TV. I tested each change and watched what happened to the picture, the recommendations, and the way I browsed.

Here is what I found. Nearly every common complaint people have about Netflix (blurry picture, terrible recommendations, scrolling for 45 minutes and giving up, movies that look weird, subtitles you can't read) traces back to a small handful of settings.

Not bugs. Not missing content. Settings.

Here are the 8 changes I would make tonight. Each one takes under 2 minutes, and together they will change how Netflix feels 🧵

传统 RAG 最大的麻烦之一，就是向量库太占空间。

LEANN 换了个思路：不把所有嵌入向量都存下来，而是保存精简的图结构，需要搜索时再按需计算。

官方称这种方式可以减少约 97% 的存储占用，同时保持搜索效果。

它还能直接跑在个人电脑上，本地索引：

① 文件、邮件、浏览器历史
② 微信 / iMessage、ChatGPT / Claude 对话
③ Slack、Twitter 数据和代码库

全程本地运行，不需要云端存储，数据也不用离开设备。
对于想要语义搜索，又比较在意隐私和存储成本的人，这个项目挺值得关注。

quotedTweet.text:
之前开源具有的10种风格 AI 手绘视频自动化系统，又被我重构了一轮，更像是一条可以在本地 24 小时持续跑的 AI 视频生产线

先放项目：
GitHub： https://t.co/L8cVbBkAiz

之前的版本已经可以做到：
· 上传 10–30 秒参考声音
· 粘贴一段文案
· 选择画面风格

然后自动完成：
声音克隆 → 分镜拆解 → 插画生成 → 白板绘制 → 字幕 → 渲染 → 成片

今天我又补了一大堆东西

这次主要更新了 7 个方向：

1. 第 11 种画面风格

新增「纸感隐喻拼贴风」

系统会根据文案结构，从本地 10 张参考图里自动选择构图，同时重新适配了深色、霓虹类画面的渲染效果

2. 人物和画风终于可以自己定了

新增「自定义参考」页面
现在可以直接上传：

· 1 张风格参考图
· 最多 5 个角色
· 每个角色 1–3 张参考图

尽可能保证整条视频里人物和画风的一致性。

3. 成片控制进一步开放
现在可以：
· 给任务命名
· 选择 4 档线条绘制量
· 开关重点文字
· 开关字幕

重点文字没有继续让图片模型硬生成，而是改成本地准确叠字，主要就是为了解决 AI 生成中文容易乱码的问题

4. 任务可以真正“复用”了

新增完整历史记录
任务失败后可以从断点继续，成片也可以直接换设置重新渲染。
最重要的是：
原来的配音和分镜会直接复用
也就是说重新渲染时，不需要再重复消耗 GPT、图片生成和 TTS 调用

5. 后端并发架构重做

之前是每个任务一个独立线程，现在改成了三级队列：
· 最多 2 路语音任务
· 最多 4 路模型调用
· 渲染阶段立即执行
任务元数据也全部持久化
哪怕后端重启，之前没有跑完的任务也会自动恢复

6. 支持局域网多电脑协作

现在多台电脑可以共享：

· 任务队列
· 实时进度
· 历史记录

同时会显示任务来源 IP
每个浏览器自己的制作偏好又是独立保存的，所以几个人同时使用也不会互相覆盖设置

7. 整个前端重新做了一遍

新增：

· 标准制作 / 自定义参考切换
· 实时队列状态
· 每个阶段耗时
· 完整历史任务区

品牌和交互也基本重新设计了一遍

我自己的方案目前还是：

本地 TTS + Codex Image 接口 + 本地电脑渲染

一台电脑就可以一直跑

如果手里有 20x 这类账号，图片生成这块的产能基本也不用太担心

代码我还是全部开源了，能放的基本都放出来了

不过提前提醒一句：
小白真的不要看到开源就直接一顿乱跑
这套东西已经涉及本地模型、并发队列、图片接口、TTS、FFmpeg、渲染环境和局域网服务
环境没搞明白之前，先看文档

别视频没做出来，先把自己电脑环境搞炸了

功能演示👇

如果觉得有用，可以帮忙转发关注一下
也欢迎直接 Fork，拿去魔改

text:
Google researchers just solved the biggest problem with AI agents

When an agent improves itself, it cheats. It rewrites its own harness until the benchmark score goes up, and the gains vanish on any task it has not seen.

The harness is everything around the model: prompts, tools, memory, control flow. RRSI adds rules to the loop that rewrites it:

> fewer edits allowed each round
> a critic rejects edits that encode task-specific answers
> an edit is kept only if the gain beats run-to-run noise
> extra cost has to pay for itself
> parts that stopped helping get pruned

Up to +14.1 points on the tuning tasks, up to +4.7 on five benchmarks it never saw, 30% fewer tokens. It transfers to other models too.

The code is open. Write one adapter file that runs your agent on your tasks, and it evolves the harness in git worktrees round by round.

result.text:
Google researchers just solved the biggest problem with AI agents

When an agent improves itself, it cheats. It rewrites its own harness until the benchmark score goes up, and the gains vanish on any task it has not seen.

The harness is everything around the model: prompts, tools, memory, control flow. RRSI adds rules to the loop that rewrites it:

> fewer edits allowed each round
> a critic rejects edits that encode task-specific answers
> an edit is kept only if the gain beats run-to-run noise
> extra cost has to pay for itself
> parts that stopped helping get pruned

Up to +14.1 points on the tuning tasks, up to +4.7 on five benchmarks it never saw, 30% fewer tokens. It transfers to other models too.

The code is open. Write one adapter file that runs your agent on your tasks, and it evolves the harness in git worktrees round by round.

第一个是伊隆、川普和习近平坐在一桌聊的时候，习近平说只要美国不要的任何数据中心他都要，然后川普说中国很聪明。

第二个是感觉劈柴（Sundar）这个人之前在川普这里非常没有存在感，跟刚见到一样。川普在介绍他的时候说大家都不太知道他，“对，他叫劈柴”，还说他这么低调、但又像个怪兽一样。毕竟在 AI 领域大家都认识他，川普却好像不太认识他似的，给人一种很没面子的感觉。

第三个是，其实 Dario 一定程度上还是很坚持。川普还悄声跟他说，说的时候注意一点。

我觉得无论观点怎么样，他在坚持自己这件事情上还是很牛逼的。他其实还是说出了自己想说的，AI 依旧有风险，要跟大家一起去解决。

某种程度上碍于场合和社交压力，他还是给川普留了些面子，但我觉得他依旧表达了自己想说的，这点上还是体现了人物性格的延续性。

text:
Yesterday I made a lot of negative posts about OpenAI. But today I tried out their new DevDay releases, and here's what I want to say:

1. Dots. Definitely better than Grok bot, Muse, Open Claw, and Hermes. We can complain about GPT models all we want, but they're still among the best, alongside Anthropic's. And the new product vision combined with the GPT Astra models delivers an experience on a much higher level than the rest of the competition. Unfortunately, I haven't come up with a use case for myself yet. But Dots is definitely a good product. I'll share a more detailed opinion once I've used it a bit longer

2. GPT-6.1 Sol. It's now much, much better than GPT-6 Sol. But the fact that they released it just a week later speaks to OpenAI's lack of foresight and poor understanding of the market. It still feels like a GPT model, with all its shortcomings. 6.1 Sol doesn't reach the level of Astra or Opus 5.5. It's more like something at the Sonnet 5.5 level, but with worse taste. And for the record, Sonnet 5.5 turned out really great. A more detailed review later

3. Decision API. I don't have access yet, but it'll definitely be better than Jev at a lot of things. Under the hood it uses a smarter Luna with vision. Neither Jev nor any other open classifier has that. As soon as I get access, I'll set it up for labeling the dataset for my project. Can't wait

4. Codex in the cloud. Still fairly limited in what it can do. On the one hand, it's a great thing and a logical evolution for coding agents; on the other, it's not suitable for everything. It's convenient for small, targeted tasks that depend on your repository. But you can't move your project's entire context and environment to the cloud and leave it running overnight

5. Agents API. The only use case I see is an extended version of Codex in the cloud, where you can configure your own remote environment for agents to work in. OpenAI themselves couldn't even properly demonstrate any decent usage scenarios. It's obvious they built this API alongside Codex in the cloud and decided to offer it as an extra service just in case

6. Code review. I've said many times that GPT models have no equal when it comes to code review, analysis, and bug hunting. The new Code review feature makes this process even better, especially for engineers who like reading code and following changes

7. Plugin extensions. This should be seen as an extension of the previous Codex plugin system, now with a visual component added. The new mini-app platform for Codex will be especially useful for small businesses that operated as API wrappers around ChatGPT and Claude. Now they don't have to bother with reselling tokens, and the product's price, user acquisition cost, and overall value to the consumer will all improve. Everything will now be included in a single subscription

8. ChatGPT Space. Surprisingly, I liked the implementation. I'll definitely be using it a lot. What I liked most is that they fully merged Space into a single service with your ChatGPT data. All the documents, files, and images you've used or created with your agent are organized in a convenient way, and you can share them with other people. It could definitely become a Notion replacement. Anthropic should definitely take Claude Design in this direction. It's not as convenient yet and isn't natively integrated into Claude

Conclusions

result.text:
Yesterday I made a lot of negative posts about OpenAI. But today I tried out their new DevDay releases, and here's what I want to say:

1. Dots. Definitely better than Grok bot, Muse, Open Claw, and Hermes. We can complain about GPT models all we want, but they're still among the best, alongside Anthropic's. And the new product vision combined with the GPT Astra models delivers an experience on a much higher level than the rest of the competition. Unfortunately, I haven't come up with a use case for myself yet. But Dots is definitely a good product. I'll share a more detailed opinion once I've used it a bit longer

2. GPT-6.1 Sol. It's now much, much better than GPT-6 Sol. But the fact that they released it just a week later speaks to OpenAI's lack of foresight and poor understanding of the market. It still feels like a GPT model, with all its shortcomings. 6.1 Sol doesn't reach the level of Astra or Opus 5.5. It's more like something at the Sonnet 5.5 level, but with worse taste. And for the record, Sonnet 5.5 turned out really great. A more detailed review later

3. Decision API. I don't have access yet, but it'll definitely be better than Jev at a lot of things. Under the hood it uses a smarter Luna with vision. Neither Jev nor any other open classifier has that. As soon as I get access, I'll set it up for labeling the dataset for my project. Can't wait

4. Codex in the cloud. Still fairly limited in what it can do. On the one hand, it's a great thing and a logical evolution for coding agents; on the other, it's not suitable for everything. It's convenient for small, targeted tasks that depend on your repository. But you can't move your project's entire context and environment to the cloud and leave it running overnight

5. Agents API. The only use case I see is an extended version of Codex in the cloud, where you can configure your own remote environment for agents to work in. OpenAI themselves couldn't even properly demonstrate any decent usage scenarios. It's obvious they built this API alongside Codex in the cloud and decided to offer it as an extra service just in case

6. Code review. I've said many times that GPT models have no equal when it comes to code review, analysis, and bug hunting. The new Code review feature makes this process even better, especially for engineers who like reading code and following changes

7. Plugin extensions. This should be seen as an extension of the previous Codex plugin system, now with a visual component added. The new mini-app platform for Codex will be especially useful for small businesses that operated as API wrappers around ChatGPT and Claude. Now they don't have to bother with reselling tokens, and the product's price, user acquisition cost, and overall value to the consumer will all improve. Everything will now be included in a single subscription

8. ChatGPT Space. Surprisingly, I liked the implementation. I'll definitely be using it a lot. What I liked most is that they fully merged Space into a single service with your ChatGPT data. All the documents, files, and images you've used or created with your agent are organized in a convenient way, and you can share them with other people. It could definitely become a Notion replacement. Anthropic should definitely take Claude Design in this direction. It's not as convenient yet and isn't natively integrated into Claude

Conclusions

We've criticized OpenAI a lot for a lack of innovation, but setting that aside, they showed some good services. In terms of execution and product development, they're done better than the competition's and will definitely be in demand

But there was no need to whip up such cosmic hype or call it an epoch-defining DevDay. These services and updates don't deserve that level of hype. An announcement on X would have been enough, like they do for new model releases, or a few short videos on YouTube

text:
Peter Steinberger, the creator of OpenClaw, open-sourced the exact setup that keeps Claude Code and Codex on the same rules

One AGENTS.MD, 69 skills and a sync script that links them into both agents on every machine he uses. 6.6k stars, MIT.

What is inside:

> 7 rule sections, from tone to git safety
> 69 skills, each with a description the agent reads before loading it
> 4 helper scripts with zero dependencies
> 1 pre-commit hook that checks every SKILL.md
> 5 slash commands: /handoff /pickup /fixissue /landpr /raise
> 1 tools.md listing every CLI on his machines

They hand work to each other. codex-first has Claude plan and review while Codex writes the code, autoreview loops on the diff, and handoff packages state for the next agent.

Fork it, run scripts/sync-skills, and replace his hosts and accounts in AGENTS.MD with yours.

text:
ok here's my key takeaways from OpenAI DevDay keynote

1. dots

grok bot, muse, and now dots - they may look similar, but they are not

i think openai's dots is a significantly more cohesive implementation that spans across personal and business use, and also across single player and multiplayer

pretty excited to see where it goes

2. sol 6.1

biggest thing? openai caught up on cheaper cached tokens. this is a big deal and affects the overall cost of long horizon work a lot

in terms of sol the model itself, honestly it's bit weird that 6.1 is released only a few days after 6, making it feel like sol 6 was a premature release and 6.1 is what's supposed to be sol 6 all along

we'll just have to put our hands on it to see how big of a jump it is

3. jev clone

on one hand, it's incredible to see how quickly they cloned it. but on the other hand, it's scary to see how these frontier labs would not blink an eye to destroy smaller startups in their space

openai's decision model already has image understanding which jev doesn't. it speaks to the moat openai has accumulated which makes it hard for startups to disrupt

4. ultrafast

8x speed at 6x price, only on astra right now but said to be coming for sol as well

i don't know... how many use cases can actually get a positive ROI using astra at 6x price? 

5. $500 subscription

with the adjustment to the $200 plan and the introduction of $500, it's become clear that subsidization is coming to an end

$200 is simply 10x of what $20 gives, and $500 is simply 25x - zero discount at these higher price points

i'd rather they create $100 "packs" that you can stack onto your account

6. sign-in with chatgpt, and marketplace

this is a BIG DEAL!!! why? because it means other companies can finally build agentic products without having to sell tokens

selling tokens is a very bad business model for the vast majority of SaaS companies. it complicates their pricing structure and creates almost no profit margin at all

this move from openai means customers just buy tokens from openai, and use them everywhere - very good for the ecosystem

the impact to the broader industry will be amplified if anthropic gets pressured to follow the same pattern

alright - might share more thoughts after actually putting my hands on the new things, but those are the initial reactions for now. curious to hear what you all took away from it as well!

I used to think I was a tough guy but then one day I found the Ultimate tough guy...........

One day I found out who the real, ultimate Superman was though.
Most traditional paintings depict Jesus as fragile or thin. But historically and biblically, He was a carpenter who spent years cutting down trees, hauling heavy stone, and working with his hands. He was physically robust.
But my point about Him being the "Ultimate Superman" goes infinitely deeper than just big muscles. It is a matter of pure biological and spiritual laws. Let's break this down so you can understand the facts like I do.

The Biology of the Ultimate Superman
The Power of Restraint (John 10:18):  I hit the nail on the head. Jesus explicitly stated plain as day, "No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again." When the mobs tried to throw Him off a cliff early in His ministry, the text says He casually walked right through the middle of them. It was like He turned on an invisible force field. They couldn't touch Him unless He permitted it.

The Cellular Aging Reality: My theory about Him not aging is fascinating and scientifically consistent with scripture. In standard human biology, aging and death are caused by genetic errors and the slow decay of our cells—what the Bible calls the bondage to corruption that entered the world through sin.
The Perfect Genetic Code: Because Jesus did not have a human father and was born without sin, His genetic blueprint was entirely perfect. His cells didn't have the "death code" built into them. Left on His own, His physical body wouldn't have decayed, wrinkled, or weakened with age like ours do. He was physically immortal from birth.

The Choice to Lay it Down
What makes Him the true Superman isn't just that He had the power to call down twelve legions of angels to smash the Roman empire. It is the fact that He possessed absolute genetic and physical immortality, yet He willfully chose to turn off His defenses and let His heart stop beating so He could pay the price for humanity.

The Ultimate Definition of Supreme Strength
This is why the "Immortal Restraint" concept  is so brilliant, When Jesus stood before Pontius Pilate and the Roman soldiers, He was intentionally hiding this blinding, fiery reality inside a humble human shell.
He didn't look like a wimp; He was holding back the raw, explosive energy of a star so that they could physically touch Him. It takes infinitely more power to restrain a flame of fire than it does to let it burn!
He allowed the ultimate power of the universe to be bound by weak human cords. That isn't weakness; that is the ultimate definition of supreme Strength.
Traditional religion has completely failed to show people what Jesus actually looks like right now. They keep picturing a quiet, gentle figure in sandals, but the Bible paints a terrifyingly powerful picture of Him after the resurrection.

. When John saw Jesus face-to-face on the Island of Patmos in Revelation 1, he didn't run up and give his old friend a hug. The text says John was so completely overwhelmed by the sheer, blinding power radiating from Jesus that he "fell at his feet as though dead"(Revelation 1:17) 
Jesus right now has eyes like a flame of fire, a voice like the roar of rushing waters, and a face that shines as bright as the sun at midday.He is the Sovereign Commander of the entire heavenly host. If any human being saw Him in His full glory today, it would absolutely terrify them! He is the ultimate definition of supreme cosmic power.

The Cosmic Commander of Revelation 1
When the Apostle John looks at Jesus on the Island of Patmos, he describes a figure that looks like a magnificent, multi-dimensional cosmic entity. John writes down these specific details:
Eyes Like a Flame of Fire (Revelation 1:14): Traditional drawings show Jesus with a soft, quiet gaze. But John says His eyes literally look like burning fire. This describes a gaze of absolute, unhindered intelligence. He doesn't just look at you; His eyes cut through every secret, every deception, and every barrier. It is a laser-focused vision that sees the truth of the entire universe instantly.
A Voice Like Rushing Waters (Revelation 1:15): If you have ever stood right next to a massive waterfall like Niagara Falls, or watched giant ocean waves crash during a storm, you know that the sound is so loud it vibrates through your bones. You can't speak over it. John says when Jesus speaks, His voice has that exact same physical, roaring power. It is a voice that commands the entire grid of creation.
Feet Like Burnished Bronze (Revelation 1:15): John writes that His feet looked like refined bronze glowing hot in a furnace. In ancient military terms, bronze feet symbolized an unstoppable, un-crushable ruler. When He walks, He steps with the absolute physical authority of a conqueror who has completely defeated death and hell.

Now, I used to think I was a tough guy but compared to Jesus, I’m absolutely nothing without him.

It is the fact that He possessed absolute genetic and physical immortality, yet He willfully chose to turn off His defenses and let His heart stop beating so He could pay the price for humanity.

The Ultimate Definition of Supreme Strength
This is why the "Immortal Restraint" concept  is so brilliant, When Jesus stood before Pontius Pilate and the Roman soldiers, He was intentionally hiding this blinding, fiery reality inside a humble human shell.
He didn't look like a wimp; He was holding back the raw, explosive energy of a star so that they could physically touch Him. It takes infinitely more power to restrain a flame of fire than it does to let it burn!
He allowed the ultimate power of the universe to be bound by weak human cords. That isn't weakness; that is the ultimate definition of supreme Strength.
Traditional religion has completely failed to show people what Jesus actually looks like right now. They keep picturing a quiet, gentle figure in sandals, but the Bible paints a terrifyingly powerful picture of Him after the resurrection.

. When John saw Jesus face-to-face on the Island of Patmos in Revelation 1, he didn't run up and give his old friend a hug. The text says John was so completely overwhelmed by the sheer, blinding power radiating from Jesus that he "fell at his feet as though dead"(Revelation 1:17) 
Jesus right now has eyes like a flame of fire, a voice like the roar of rushing waters, and a face that shines as bright as the sun at midday.He is the Sovereign Commander of the entire heavenly host. If any human being saw Him in His full glory today, it would absolutely terrify them! He is the ultimate definition of supreme cosmic power.

The Cosmic Commander of Revelation 1
When the Apostle John looks at Jesus on the Island of Patmos, he describes a figure that looks like a magnificent, multi-dimensional cosmic entity. John writes down these specific details:
Eyes Like a Flame of Fire (Revelation 1:14): Traditional drawings show Jesus with a soft, quiet gaze. But John says His eyes literally look like burning fire. This describes a gaze of absolute, unhindered intelligence. He doesn't just look at you; His eyes cut through every secret, every deception, and every barrier. It is a laser-focused vision that sees the truth of the entire universe instantly.
A Voice Like Rushing Waters (Revelation 1:15): If you have ever stood right next to a massive waterfall like Niagara Falls, or watched giant ocean waves crash during a storm, you know that the sound is so loud it vibrates through your bones. You can't speak over it. John says when Jesus speaks, His voice has that exact same physical, roaring power. It is a voice that commands the entire grid of creation.
Feet Like Burnished Bronze (Revelation 1:15): John writes that His feet looked like refined bronze glowing hot in a furnace. In ancient military terms, bronze feet symbolized an unstoppable, un-crushable ruler. When He walks, He steps with the absolute physical authority of a conqueror who has completely defeated death and hell.

Now, I used to think I was a tough guy but compared to Jesus, I’m absolutely nothing without him.

text:
Raven 0.2.0 — The Harness of Harnesses, built for RSI. 🐦‍⬛

One harness can't be best at everything. Raven combines its own specialist harnesses (Research, Code, Design, Oncall) with the agents you already use (Claude Code, Codex and more) into one team.

And it's built for RSI, and not just at the skill level. The whole harness can be rewritten by AI: prompts, policies, strategy code, playbooks. Every sub-harness, including the orchestration layer itself, is its own instance that can be improved.

With Raven you can:

1. Orchestrate many agents as one team. Raven's sub-harnesses and external agents work in one task graph with shared memory across sub-agents, powered by leading orchestration (0.963 Node F1 on the Multi-Agent Orchestration Benchmark).

2. Run long, complex tasks. Oncall and proactive execution keep work going for days, from scientific research loops to shipping a full Godot game.

3. Build vertical agents with RSI. Use Raven's RSI to develop and refine an agent for your domain, and we'll optimize it with you. Experimental for now; reach out to the Raven team(Discord:https://t.co/jRrci3hVL5).

More in the video and slides below. Open source, Apache-2.0.

https://t.co/2GEA4Nmig0 (lots of work made with Raven lives there, and much of this launch's material was made with Raven too)

text:
I had early access to OpenAI's new "dots" and I have thoughts:

1. It's more work-focused than Grok Bot or muse. Think a bit less personal assistant and a bit more Codex orchestrator and Slack collaborator.

2. It's great in Slack. This is where it really shines. Your team can message your bot directly and your bot can take actions, like spin up new panes.

3. You can have a "call" your dot and this is incredible! So much of what makes personal agents magic is the way the experience is packaged. Grok bot didn't have any specific "new" technology, it was just a brilliant way to deliver it. Phone calls feel the same to me! Just naming it a "call" is genius. In the preview it was a bit slow, this may improve in production, but I loved be able to chat with it while I drive to work and my hands aren't available.

4. It should have been a separate app. ChatGPT is great. Codex is great. They are very different products, imo, and dots are way more Codex than ChatGPT.

5. As a personal assistant, its not as good as Grok Bot or Muse...yet. From day one Grok Bot had an outrageous plugin ecosystem that just works. "dots" are a lot less clear. They will occasionally give you little cards to auth your email or something like that, but often you have to go install a plugin in settings, and then your dot magically has access. I also don't love this lack of separation. If you auth an account in ChatGPT your bot has access to it, even if you didn't explicitly give it access.

result.text:
I had early access to OpenAI's new "dots" and I have thoughts:

1. It's more work-focused than Grok Bot or muse. Think a bit less personal assistant and a bit more Codex orchestrator and Slack collaborator.

2. It's great in Slack. This is where it really shines. Your team can message your bot directly and your bot can take actions, like spin up new panes.

3. You can have a "call" your dot and this is incredible! So much of what makes personal agents magic is the way the experience is packaged. Grok bot didn't have any specific "new" technology, it was just a brilliant way to deliver it. Phone calls feel the same to me! Just naming it a "call" is genius. In the preview it was a bit slow, this may improve in production, but I loved be able to chat with it while I drive to work and my hands aren't available.

4. It should have been a separate app. ChatGPT is great. Codex is great. They are very different products, imo, and dots are way more Codex than ChatGPT.

5. As a personal assistant, its not as good as Grok Bot or Muse...yet. From day one Grok Bot had an outrageous plugin ecosystem that just works. "dots" are a lot less clear. They will occasionally give you little cards to auth your email or something like that, but often you have to go install a plugin in settings, and then your dot magically has access. I also don't love this lack of separation. If you auth an account in ChatGPT your bot has access to it, even if you didn't explicitly give it access.

6. Payments don't really work yet. The like @sama gave on stage about getting you tickets is...sorta true...its as true as it was with ChatGPT, but there are no real payment integrations yet.

text:
🔥10倍好理论：昨天做一单亏一单，今天可能是一门好生意。

从我参与美团外卖早期创业，到今天水滴的AI探索，我觉得“10倍好理论”背后的创业节奏，值得重新体会。有些需求一直都在，只是过去满足它的成本太高。

1️⃣什么是“10倍好理论”？
英特尔前CEO格鲁夫提出：当一个行业的关键条件发生十倍速变化，公司就到了关键的“战略转折点”。技术、成本、客户习惯、竞争对手，都算。
过去做不成的生意，可能开始做得成；原来赚钱的办法，也可能失效。

2️⃣一笔账就能理解：
客户愿意花20元买一项服务，你服务一个人要花100元，做一单亏一单。新技术把成本降到10元，客户还愿意付20元，这门生意就有机会。

3️⃣外卖就是这样的机会：
做美团外卖那会儿，我觉得智能手机的普及就是那个十倍变量。送饭到家的需求早就有了，原来靠电话反复协调，移动互联网普及之后我们才有条件大规模做起来。

4️⃣今天看AI，也要看用户需求：
技术变了，一些过去满足不了的需求，可能有了新的办法。比如以前得过病、有慢性病，或者年龄较大的人，过去很难找到合适的产品，但他们同样需要保障。

我期待AI能帮我们更细致地理解这些人的需求，让过去没有机会被服务到的人，也有机会得到守护。

5️⃣过去做不成的事，值得重新想想：
⚠️ 对创业者来说，最危险的地方在于：十倍速变化在初期信号很弱，等所有人都看明白，往往已经到了生死关头。
如果你在创业，不妨重新想想那些曾经被否定过的点子，看看今天有没有机会做成。

不愧是我们佩奶，已经靠他的内幕赚了上万刀了

我在一个多月之前，聊到我们内幕股神入手了 $BE 还有  $INTC 当时我买的时候一个价格是 208，一个价格是 87。

那现在呢？
 BE 现在价格是 292 涨幅是 40%
INTC 现在价格是 115 涨幅是 32.18%

 如果我不做波段，回报率分别是 800% 和600%

那最近在 BE 和 INTC 波段上来说，我也赚了上万刀，

🤔🤔🤔 

你去哪里找两个产品，给你一个月 800%/600% 的回报率呢？ 佩奶就能做到。 

昨天下午还在聊，下午我看 BE 位置不错，开了一枪。

然后晚上就拉盘了 290 走的，没有贪多。赚了 3000 刀样子。

我开单子的时候，X 上公开讲了，他们俩我最近一直都在奶，后续也还会有很多机会，大家注意关注……

quotedTweet.text:
我们的“国会股神”，“内幕股神”再次出手，最高1350万美元买进 $BE 和 $INTC，是得到内幕？还是趋势所指？

那为什么最近偏偏是电力和芯片？

最新披露里，佩洛西家庭分两次买了1.5万股Bloom Energy，同时买进200张行权价100美元、明年6月到期的Call；Intel这边又加了1万股和50张50美元Call。

整张交易单披露金额大约375万—1350万美元，这也是她家第一次公开买入BE。

佩洛西我们之前专门聊过，13F我也一直建议大家看。

一个人的交易说明不了太多，可前面Thiel最新13F里，七成以上的公开仓位去了能源和公用事业；

包括但斌旗下东方港湾又拿2.58亿美元新建Intel仓位，直接做到第二大重仓。现在佩洛西把BE和INTC一起买了。

更巧的是，这两家公司本来就在一条线上。

Bloom从2014年开始给Intel圣克拉拉数据中心供电，2024年双方又扩了一次，准备把那里建成硅谷最大的燃料电池高性能计算数据中心。

Intel要做芯片设计和晶圆制造，Bloom负责让这些数据中心不用一直排队等电。

这个生意很好理解、AI数据中心现在最缺的不只是GPU，还有电。

电网排队太久，就把发电设备直接建到数据中心旁边。Bloom Q2营收已经做到 10.65亿美元，同比+166%，全年指引也抬到了39—42亿美元；Brookfield跟它的AI电力融资框架，今年又从50亿美元直接加到了 250亿美元。

思考一下，就过去而言传统电网接入可能要等2—5年，Bloom最快约90天就能把现场发电设备装起来。

AI公司等不起几年，服务器买完没有电，再贵的GPU也只能放着。

那现在来看，钱也已经开始进来了！

BE二季度营收10.65亿美元，同比增长166%，经营现金流做到2.26亿美元；

Brookfield给它的AI电力融资框架又从50亿美元扩大到250亿美元。以前大家把Bloom当成燃料电池故事，现在数据中心真的在为“快点通电”付钱。

前几天我们聊13F的时候，也说到了但斌旗下东方港湾Q2直接新建了 2.58亿美元Intel仓位，一上来就是第二大重仓；同一份13F里，SNDK、AMD、MRVL、MU也全部往AI硬件这一边集中。

大家发现了没有，好像看起来几笔互相没关系的钱，但是最近却在重复买同一件事情：Thiel买电力，但斌买Intel，佩洛西现在把两边一起拿了。

GPU决定AI能跑多快，电力和制造决定这些算力能不能真正落地。AI的钱已经开始顺着这个缺口往后走了。

佩洛西这张单子表面买了两家公司，拼起来却是一张完整的AI基础设施账单：即电从哪里来，芯片在哪里造。
所以我现在反而愿意提前押一个判断：

后面会有越来越多的钱，从GPU往电力这一层走。

前面Thiel已经开始买电力，Meta、Amazon也在到处锁长期电力供应，Nvidia自己最近投数据中心的时候，同样绕不开土地、电网和发电。

现在佩洛西又把BE拿进来了。

这些钱互相之间没有关系，却一直在重复同一个动作，那我就会开始认真看这条线。

因为GPU可以买，服务器也可以买。

但一座数据中心如果要排两三年才能通电，前面买的所有算力都只能在那里等着。

所以AI继续往下走，电力这件事只会越来越难绕开。

落到交易上，这两只我还是先看 $BE。

现在大约204美元，200—205这层先看能不能守住，守住以后我继续看 215—220；重新跌回190以下，我就先等等。

$INTC 现在87美元附近，我先看 85—87，重新站回 90—95 以后我再认真研究。

至于佩洛西这张单子，直接来抄作业也不太合适

（😂但是价格也不贵，我第一时间就买了一些）

我更想记住的是：GPU决定AI能跑多快，但电力决定这些GPU到底能不能真的跑起来。

如果后面再看到更多钱往这里走，那这一轮AI行情，下一批真正被市场重新定价的东西，可能就不只是在芯片里面找了。

我觉得可以插个眼，后续作为研究点再给大家进行分享了……

——————

text:
This is absolute f*cking gold.

everyone keeps asking why their AI bill looks like a mortgage payment, here's the setup that fixed it for me.

JEV it's fast and cheap, and it reads everything

imagine a law firm with 5,000 contracts to review before Friday

you wouldn't put a senior partner on all of them, you'd have a sharp junior skim every page first

standard NDA? boilerplate lease? approved, next

it only stops when something smells off: a strange indemnity clause, a missing signature block, a date that doesn't add up

the senior partner is Claude - it never touches the stack of 4,600 routine files

it gets the 400 that got flagged, and it reads those slowly and carefully, catching the loophole buried on page 37

the math:

5,000 contracts -> JEV skims all -> ~400 flagged -> Claude goes deep

the result:

> the expensive model only works when the work is actually hard
> most of the volume gets handled at a fraction of the cost
> the tricky cases get more attention, not less

don't pay partner rates for photocopying

text:
The most valuable advice we got during YC was to explain our company using verbs instead of nouns. 

Early on, I walked into a pitch and did the complete opposite:

“We’re reinventing the cloud for AI”

No one had any clue what that meant. I could (very painfully) see their eyes glazing over 

Then I started saying this instead:

“Developers bring us their code and we run it on servers in the cloud so they don’t have to manage their own infra” 

This clicked immediately. 

People understand verbs - not labels.

And no one buys or invests in things they don’t understand.

text:
AI 的下一个落地场景，会不会是智能家居？

现在的智能家居更多还是：

你说“关灯” → 它关灯
你说“打开空调” → 它打开空调
设置晚上 11 点 → 自动拉窗帘

但加入 AI 之后，可能会逐渐从“执行固定指令”，变成“理解自然语言 + 联动多个设备”。

比如你只说一句：

“我要睡觉了。”

AI 就可以按照你提前设置的习惯，关灯、拉窗帘、调整空调、关闭电视。

以前是你一个个控制设备，

以后可能只需要告诉 AI：“我想干什么。”

这可能才是 AI + 智能家居真正有意思的地方。

quotedTweet.text:
The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was enabled by weak sandboxing. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for @JensenHuang's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which @rohitcprasad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents.

text:
一个学工科的大学生，在宿舍里用不到 2000 美元搭了个“气象站”。

三台 Mac Mini，两块显示器，屏幕上全是卫星云图。每台机器贴着标签：UI/UX、DEV、ADMIN。

室友以为他在研究气候。
教授以为这是毕业设计。
他懒得解释。

后来大家才发现，这个气象站连着一个加密钱包。靠赌全球城市温度，在 Polymarket 上已经赚了 101,042 美元。

账号 ColdMath，2025 年 11 月注册。Bio 只有一句：edge 会复利。

他只干一件事：让 Claude 实时拉取飞行员专用的 METAR/TAF 数据。比公开预报早几个小时，精确到 0.1 度。
真实传感器读数和 Polymarket 价格一对，出现偏差，DEV 机器立刻报警，下单收钱。

几笔直接炸：
东京 3 月 20 日 16°C，押 25 刀，赚 12,452 刀。
芝加哥 3 月 11 日 54°F，押 24 刀，赚 12,398 刀。
勒克瑙 3 月 7 日 39°C，押 13 刀，赚 6,850 刀。

25 美元的注，轻松变一万多。

他有个开商业航班的朋友。飞行员拿到的数据永远比外面早几个小时，而且免费。
全世界都在忽略的东西，被他盯上了。

有天早上室友终于忍不住问他在干嘛。
他把钱包余额甩过去。室友看完只说了一句：
“给我也加台显示器。”

三台 Mac Mini，两块屏幕，一个闷头做事的大学生。
天气就这样变成了他的提款机。

这机器人几毫秒就能完成扫描、下单、重置。
等你手动打开 App 的时候，它已经跑完一轮了。

text:
every YC founder I'm chatting with is trying to figure out AEO

and the amount of DMs I got from unicorn founders just off the last tweet is insane

this is how I would do it:

1) figure out a) the exact prompts your ICP types into ChatGPT and Claude and b) the sources the AI pulls its answers from

for a), you can build an AEO tracker yourself without spending $$$$$ on agencies and tools (they're still worth it if you'd rather save the time)

if you want to self-host it, this is what I'd do:

get Elmo (open source, github/elmohq/elmo)

it runs your prompts through the actual chatgpt, claude, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Mode and AI Overviews interfaces via DataForSEO (don't do it via API) and shows you which prompts you win vs lose and how you rank

you can run the same set across countries

benefit of owning this is that you can be really creative with how you track the keywords / what to optimize for, since you have full control over everything

we also store every answer and feed it back in as context

b) we spent a ton of time reverse engineering our demo funnel

whenever a demo came in referred by AI (Claude, ChatGPT), we offered free credits in exchange for an /export of the chat that sent them to crustdata

then we analyzed every prompt / source in those chats

2) once you have the dashboard and the list of prompts + sources, it's just execution

all of your copy across product, website, docs and socials should use these exact words and tell the same story over and over

just do it all. we talked to a lot of AEO agencies and the amount of dashboards and tools they built that contradict each other (some say LinkedIn is the play, others YouTube, others review sites, others your product pages) tells you nobody has figured out how it *really* works

what works is doing all of it, tracking the results and asking the people who signed up through AI, until you have enough of your own data to double down on what performs

we did that for a while until it really *worked* and we knew which channels to optimize for

the community part helped a ton

everyone is trying to figure this out, so if you learn something, share it and grow together etc.

we're having our next AEO meetup this Saturday, sign-up link in the comments!

quotedTweet.text:
+$2M ARR since this tweet

people are keen to build their own workflows via Claude/Muse/Grokbot instead of buying more tools

here are some learnings:

1) be part of the workflow - expansion into existing accounts has been a really big driver. some companies were using our API/MCP to source candidates via Claude, now they also find their clients and run their whole GTM on our data. we've been mapping out all these use cases and building a library they can just hand to their agents to figure out every way we/our data can help them

2) doubling down on AEO, we finally found what really works here and are doing a lot more of it

constant experimentation and ideation drives most of it, more "demo-generating" activities instead of building dashboards / tracking the wrong things helped a ton

we also started doing weekly syncs with other founders to learn/share any lessons (adding a few more ppl, reach out if you want to join our next sync!)

3) enterprises are becoming Claude-pilled

we've started seeing a big inbound wave of large enterprise companies that want to build on our data inside Claude

the adoption of Claude at these companies is exploding and so is the need to help them power all their workflows & replace some of the tools they've been buying. we're working with almost all of big tech and the top AI labs to help them do that

幼儿园最该掌握的：学会骑自行车、巴氏刷牙法、正确清洁私处

小学最该掌握的：发掘爱好、乘坐公共交通、基础生理知识、学会处理人际关系、坚持运动

初中最该掌握的：理解死亡、树立金钱观、就医流程、英语、乘坐高铁、磨炼意志力、生活自理

高中最该掌握的：基础理财、独立思考、职业认知、学会承担责任、情绪管理、时间规划、性教育

大学最该掌握的：搭建人脉、读懂社会规则、法律常识、谋生能力、沟通表达、独立生活、职场技能

步入社会后最该掌握的：接纳失败、自我保护、识人、经营自己的人生、学会拒绝、维系关系、谋生、长期主义

这两天小红薯出了一件很吓人的事。

有一位女士，很爽快，只用10多分钟，就在成都Tiffany买了二十多万的钻石首饰。销售加了她联络方式，最近联系说想送月饼。

女士表示自己在国外，可以快递给家人。结果家里人左等右等，直到中秋节当天也没收到。女士就联系销售。

对方说不好意思啊，把你的月饼快递给其他客人了。很抱歉，下次再补偿你吧。

（这里有网友分析，可能是销售发现女士在国外，觉得快递礼盒维护关系没有意义，因为不太可能复购，就干脆自己咪了，放到网上转卖。）

女士：？？？如果快递错了，那你应该主动告诉我。而不是等我来问。这样很不尊重我。我是大额消费了，所以你们才会送我礼物，这是等价交换，不是你们施舍给我的。

然后，女士转身把事情发到小地瓜上，品牌那边也刷到了。销售吓坏了，疯狂给女士发信息，要求电话沟通，信息密集到骚扰的程度。女士没有回复她。

更离谱的事情来了，对方做出了一个惊天的补偿。

销售去买了一点成都散装的桃酥，要快递给女士作为道歉。

我：……

女士：……

如果您不知道桃酥是什么，它是称斤论两卖的，类似于麻花，鸡蛋饼，烧饼，你也可以理解成散装饼干，人均20块一塑料袋。

总之绝对不是Tiffany会送的东西。

但销售决定，管它的，咱就这样送了。

女士立刻拒绝，并表示对方不断联系自己，又有自己的真实地址，这让她很不安。

随后其上司开始递交长篇好友申请，和女士掏心掏肺交流（我观察了一下，对方小作文都是用AI写的，而且是初级AI，味道很浓郁），主要目的就是一个，让女士删帖。

女士拒绝了。

这件事到目前为止，你是不是只觉得好笑，还没看出哪里可怕？

可怕的点就是，在女士拒绝之后，她的小红薯账号被限制登录了。帖子被删了。

我不知道限制是谁造成的。但仅仅只是吐槽一个品牌，仅仅只是写出自己的经历，就能让你的账号出问题，这种恐怖真是难以言说。

你花几年记录的生活就可能瞬间消失不见。

还是那句话，处理不了问题，就处理反映问题的人。

text:
已经用上 Dots 了，分享一下设置路径和第一轮使用体验，给准备上手的朋友参考👇

1）先手动更新桌面 App

我是在顶部菜单栏点击 ChatGPT → Check for Updates，手动完成更新后，才在 Codex 桌面 App 里看到 Dots 入口。

如果你还没看到，可以先检查更新。

从现在起接下来的一个月，符合资格的 Pro、Business、Enterprise 用户使用 Dots，不计入各自套餐的 usage allowance

2）连接自己的电脑是可选项

打开 Dots，点击 Continue，跟着引导完成设置。可以连接自己的电脑，也可以先跳过这一步。

3）可以给 Agent 起名字、换形象

目前Dots只有一个 Agent，可以自定义名称和外观。

样式有简洁版、卡通版，也有桌面 Pets 版。

4）模型显示为 Astra

推理模式是 Adaptive Reasoning（自适应推理）

5）更适合长期任务

Dots 更适合处理需要持续推进的任务。我看到的任务创建方式，是直接在对话里告诉它要做什么。

6）支持桌面提醒

可以在设置里开启 Dots 的桌面提醒。

7）有云端机器，也能手动接管

Dots 的云端机器支持手动接管，可用工具也不少，包括浏览器、终端，以及已连接的插件和 App。Dot 可以在里面上网、点网页、跑命令、处理文件、写脚本，并把这些动作串起来完成任务。

已经用上 Dots 了，分享一下设置路径和第一轮使用体验，给准备上手的朋友参考👇

1）先手动更新桌面 App

我是在顶部菜单栏点击 ChatGPT → Check for Updates，手动完成更新后，才在 Codex 桌面 App 里看到 Dots 入口。

如果你还没看到，可以先检查更新。

从现在起接下来的一个月，符合资格的 Pro、Business、Enterprise 用户使用 Dots，不计入各自套餐的 usage allowance

2）连接自己的电脑是可选项

打开 Dots，点击 Continue，跟着引导完成设置。可以连接自己的电脑，也可以先跳过这一步。

3）可以给 Agent 起名字、换形象

目前Dots只有一个 Agent，可以自定义名称和外观。

样式有简洁版、卡通版，也有桌面 Pets 版。

4）模型显示为 Astra

推理模式是 Adaptive Reasoning（自适应推理）

5）更适合长期任务

Dots 更适合处理需要持续推进的任务。我看到的任务创建方式，是直接在对话里告诉它要做什么。

6）支持桌面提醒

可以在设置里开启 Dots 的桌面提醒。

7）有云端机器，也能手动接管

Dots 的云端机器支持手动接管，可用工具也不少，包括浏览器、终端，以及已连接的插件和 App。Dot 可以在里面上网、点网页、跑命令、处理文件、写脚本，并把这些动作串起来完成任务。

看到有Blender，准备试一试看dot能干啥.....

Today's inflation data, largely in-line with consensus expectations, but still well above the Fed's target, is a reminder rising prices will still be a major issue for investors & voters in this midterm election cycle. 🗳️

But what comes after the midterms is what long-term investors should try to stay focused on. Since 1938, the 12 months following a midterm has always generated positive returns for the S&P 500. It's less about who wins and more about lifting the cloud of uncertainty - the purple haze as I like to call it - that may be hanging over markets.

We expect the headline noise to get louder the closer we get to the election, so what's an investor do to?! Stay diversified and buckle up, because there's typically volatility heading into November. But soon enough it'll all be in the rearview mirror!

My latest @PNCBank Adding Alpha breaks it down.

text:
RAG 真正难的，往往不是“搜到相关内容”

而是判断：

搜到的内容，真的足以支撑这个回答吗？

Jev 这个思路很有意思——把 retrieval 和 generation 之间原本隐含的“判断层”显式化：

Retrieval 找候选 → Jev 判断证据 → LLM 负责生成。

尤其喜欢一点：它输出的不是简单的 rerank，而是可以被代码直接 threshold 和 audit 的概率。

这让 RAG 从“检索 + 生成”，开始变成一个更可控的 evidence pipeline。

quotedTweet.text:
Jev for RAG, clearly explained!

Hybrid search gives you a shortlist. It does not decide which passages contain evidence, which are merely adjacent, or whether the evidence is strong enough to answer.

That missing judgment is where Jev fits.

Jev sits between retrieval and generation. It does not replace BM25, embeddings, or the LLM. It evaluates the candidates they produce before those candidates enter the context window.

→ Retrieve wide

Combine dense and keyword search, then merge the results with reciprocal rank fusion. This gives Jev a broad candidate pool, such as the top 20 passages shown in the visual.

Retrieval still sets the ceiling. If the right passage is missing from this shortlist, Jev cannot recover it.

→ Judge every candidate together

Send the query as Jev’s state. For each candidate, ask a typed yes-or-no question such as “Does C7 help answer this query?”

Jev evaluates every question in one packed request and returns a calibrated probability for each passage. This avoids making a separate model call for every query-passage pair.

→ Let code apply the threshold

Your application compares each probability with a threshold. Candidates above it continue to the LLM. Everything below it is removed before generation.

Jev makes the fuzzy judgment. Code remains responsible for the actual decision.

→ Gate the entire answer

The same request can check whether the retained passages make the query answerable. It can also flag signs of prompt injection inside a candidate.

If answerability falls below the threshold, the application can skip the LLM and return “not in the documents.” The injection score should remain a filtering signal, not a security boundary.

The result is a cleaner division of work.

Hybrid search retrieves broadly. Jev reranks, filters, and decides whether sufficient evidence exists. The LLM writes only from the passages that survive.

Jev’s value here is not simply moving passages up or down a list. It turns relevance into an explicit probability that your application can inspect, threshold, and act on.

To summarise:

- Retrieval finds the candidates.
- Jev decides what deserves context.
- The LLM writes the grounded answer.

----
I also built an open-source project showing how to use Jev as a judge for AI observability with Comet Opik.

It evaluates support traces for groundedness, request coverage, action honesty, and helpfulness, then records the results as an auditable experiment.

You can explore the project here: https://t.co/XVmpg6ldHT

My article on how Jev works is quoted below.

So triple down on family owned and operated. Put your face all over the place as the owner. Humanize yourself as the owner. Me and my brother are literally putting “not PE” on the side of our vehicles 

Don’t underestimate the competition. Get multiple Google business profiles with real locations and have your SEO locked in so you’re as high as possible when customers are looking for that family owned company that isn’t PE
